title: Find All Good Strings
constraints: s1, s2 and evil consist of lowercase English letters
signature: int findGoodStrings(int n, String s1, String s2, String evil)
notes:
## Intuition

Listing every string between `s1` and `s2` and searching each for `evil` is hopeless: there can be up to 26^500 of them. Instead, build the string one letter at a time and count, like a digit DP on numbers. To place the next letter we only need three facts about the prefix so far: how many letters of `evil` its end currently matches, whether it is still equal to `s1`'s prefix (then the next letter cannot go below `s1`'s), and whether it is still equal to `s2`'s prefix (then it cannot go above `s2`'s). Strings sharing these facts behave the same from now on, so they are counted together. The KMP failure function tells how the match length changes after each letter.

## Approach

1. Build `fail`, the KMP prefix function of `evil`.
2. Build `step[j][c]`: the new match length after adding letter `c` when `j` letters were matched. A match extends to `j + 1`, otherwise fall back through `fail`.
3. `dp[j][low][high]` counts prefixes with match length `j` and the two "still equal" flags. Start with the empty prefix: `dp[0][1][1] = 1`.
4. For each position, try every letter `c` from `first` (`s1`'s letter if `low`, else `a`) to `last` (`s2`'s letter if `high`, else `z`). Skip it when `step` reaches `m` (`evil` was completed); otherwise add the count to the new state, keeping a flag only if `c` equals that bound's letter.
5. After `n` letters, add up every state.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 2`, `s1 = "aa"`, `s2 = "da"`, `evil = "b"`. At position 0 the letters `a` to `d` are allowed: `a` keeps `low`, `d` keeps `high`, `c` keeps neither, and `b` completes `evil` and is dropped. At position 1 the prefix `a` may use any letter from `a` up but `b` (25), `c` may use any letter but `b` (25), and `d` must stop at `a` (1). The total is `25 + 25 + 1 = 51`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · m · 26), with m = `evil.length`: four flag pairs and 26 letters per match length and position.
- Space: O(m · 26) for `step` plus O(m) per DP layer.

## Pitfalls

- Resetting the match to 0 on a mismatch misses overlaps: in `"aaab"` with `evil = "aab"`, the third `a` must keep 2 matched letters.
- A flag stays on only while the letter equals that bound's letter; once it drops it never returns.
- When `s1 == s2` both flags start on together, so only one string is possible.
- Take the modulus after every addition.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `m` | length of `evil` |
| `fail` | KMP prefix function: longest proper border of `evil[0..i]` |
| `step[j][c]` | match length after adding letter `c` to a match of length `j` |
| `dp`, `next` | counts per state for the current and the next position |
| `low`, `high` | 1 while the prefix equals the prefix of `s1` or `s2` |
| `first`, `last` | the range of letters allowed at this position |
| `matched` | match length after the chosen letter |
| `total` | sum of every state after the last position |
